Based on your Months summary · Review before sharing
I’ve been getting spotting, and my bleeding pattern has changed. I’ve also been taking painkillers quite often, but I still have pain.

I had spotting from 31 August to 5 September, then again on 30 September. I had bleeding from 25 to 29 September. It started light, was heavy for two days, then got lighter. I didn’t log anything from 6 to 24 September, so my records don’t show what happened during that time.

The last three times I recorded bleeding starting were 13 June, 30 July and 25 September. There were 47 days between the first two and 57 days between the next two. I’m not sure whether these were my periods or something else.

I’ve been keeping track of my sleep, meals and yoga too. Looking at my records, spotting seemed to happen more often after late nights and less often on days I did yoga. The app also noticed a possible pattern with the foods I logged, but I didn’t record all the ingredients or how much oil I used. I’m not sure whether any of these things are connected.
I took vitamin D every day from 1 to 7 September and recorded spotting on five of those days.

I wanted to ask what might be causing the spotting and these longer gaps. The painkillers I’ve been taking don’t seem to help—is there something else I could try? Would ibuprofen be suitable with the other medicines I take?
Patient-reported history for discussion. This draft does not provide a diagnosis.

Based on 3-Months summary · Review before sharing
I keep getting cramps, spotting and bloating, and I’m not sure why. Sometimes the pain interrupts my sleep or gets in the way of what I need to do.

I saw a doctor on 12 August about the cramps and spotting. In my notes, I wrote that I should keep a symptom diary and come back if the symptoms continued. I still don’t have a clear explanation, and I recorded spotting again on 20 August and 22 September.
My periods were from 3 to 7 July, 4 to 8 August and 6 to 10 September. Each lasted five days, with two heavy days in the middle. I also had spotting separately on 19 July, before that appointment.

Over those three months, I wrote about needing more rest on 24 days and having my activities interrupted on eight days. Some of those might have been the same days. I haven’t written about it every day, though.
I recorded 12 nights when pain disturbed my sleep. I felt tired the next day after nine of them, although I sometimes felt tired even when pain hadn’t disturbed my sleep.
I wondered whether skipping meals made the bloating worse. It happened on some days when I skipped a meal, but also on days when I ate regularly.
I tried stretching and checked how my cramps felt before and afterwards. Out of 18 times, they eased after 10, stayed the same after six and got worse after two.
I also took painkillers on some days when I had cramps, but I didn’t write down when I took them or whether they helped.

The symptoms are still happening, so I wanted to ask what we should look into next. What can I do when the cramps affect my sleep or stop me doing things? And what pain relief would be suitable for me?
This draft does not provide a diagnosis.

Based on your Year summary · Review before sharing
I have PCOS, and I wanted to talk about my periods, Diane-35 and some nausea I noticed after starting it.
I didn’t have any periods from October to December, when I wasn’t taking hormonal pills. I started prescribed Diane-35 in January after other treatments hadn’t helped my acne enough.

From January to September, I logged nine periods while taking it. Each lasted about five days, with lighter flow at the beginning and end and heavier flow in between. I have the exact dates in my records. I understand that having periods while taking hormonal pills doesn’t necessarily mean my natural cycle has returned.

I wrote about feeling nauseous on 4 and 8 January. By April, I noticed fewer breakouts and felt that my skin was clearer. I’m not sure whether Diane-35 caused the nausea, and I didn’t record how long it lasted or how severe it was.

I’ve also been trying to understand what helps me day to day. I seem to feel more rested when I go to bed and wake up at similar times. I felt tired in the afternoon less often when I ate lunch, and I felt more energetic after 30 of the 40 short walks I recorded. The walks usually lasted 10 to 20 minutes.
My skin seems better, but I’m worried about taking a daily pill long term. What other options would suit me? If I change or stop it with your guidance, what should I do if my periods don’t come back?
I’d also like to talk about the nausea and which daily habits are worth keeping alongside my treatment.
